name: Question 12
problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 5{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=3 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=5\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13{x}_{2} & =13\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4(1) & =3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=1$ into the third equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & =5 \\ 5(1)+2(1) & =5 \\ 7 & =5,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement. 

So, the system has no solution.

x1[−135]+x2[412]=[345][−x13x15x1]+[4x2x22x2]=[345][−x1+4x23x1+x25x1+2x2]=[345].

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system: {−x1+4x2=33x1+x2=45x1+2x2=5

Multiplying the first equation by 3 and adding the result to the second equation, we get

13x2=13⟹x2=1.

Substituting x2=1 into the first equation, we get

−x1+4(1)=3⟹x1=1.
